description: Grams of one ingredient of a dish saved for `servings` portions when `parts` portions are eaten: quantityG x parts / servings, rounded half-up to one decimal. servings <= 0 counts as 1.

cases.why: A single-portion dish applied once gives the saved quantity back unchanged.
Batch cooking: one part of a gratin saved for four portions is a quarter of each ingredient.
The ½ step of the portion stepper halves a single-portion dish.
Oil split in three gives 3.3 g, not 3.3333: one decimal, so both apps show the same figure.
0.25 g rounds half-up to 0.3 g, never banker's rounding to 0.2: the corpus-wide tie rule applies here too.
A dish saved with 0 servings (corrupt or legacy data) is read as one portion, never a division by zero.
